observed_original_abi.calling_convention: __thiscall (receiver in ECX), zero ordinary stack arguments, caller cleans the stack
observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The derived ABI record (categories.abi_derived.value) states calling_convention __thiscall with hidden_this true and hidden_this_register ECX, at confidence INFERRED, and lists __fastcall as the only other candidate. Three facts in the body corroborate the receiver and are what the declaration rests on: ECX is dereferenced by the very first instruction (0x00b8de30, MOV EAX,[ECX+0x184]) before anything writes it; the body names no stack operand anywhere, so there is no ordinary stack argument; and the terminal at 0x00b8de50 is C3, a bare RET with no imm16, so the entry pops zero bytes (categories.abi_derived.value.cleanup: bytes 0, side caller). A caller listing shows the same shape from the far side: 0x00bbe608 is `mov ecx,esi` / `call 0xb8de30` / `mov edi,eax` with nothing pushed. The __thiscall/__fastcall disjunction is not resolved here and does not need to be: no stack argument exists for __fastcall to add, so the modelled entry is one receiver parameter either way.
observed_original_abi.termination: single RET at 0x00b8de50; 0x00b8de51..0x00b8de54 is cc cc cc cc (INT3 pad), so the body cannot run past it
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: no value produced by this body. The last value-producing operation in the complete listing is CALL 0x00ba6d80, and nothing in the body then writes EAX before the RET, so whatever that callee left in EAX is what a caller sees and this body makes no statement about it. The derived record is explicit that the width is not determinable here: return_semantics 'unclassified_in_EAX', and inference RT2 registers the last EAX write as register_class 'aggregate_unknown'.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: NOT a claim that the machine returns nothing. The validator's own must-analysis classes this shape UNCLASSIFIED (the last value-producing op is a CALL), so the machine offers no return verdict for this target whatever the source declares. No typedef of the record's register-class vocabulary was written to make a comparison succeed. READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE VERDICT: the committed knowledge-index record for 0x00b8de30 carries abi {}, so before this sidecar existed RETURN SEMANTICS was NOT_AVAILABLE (no canonical return_type in any ABI layer). This sidecar's observed_original_abi.return_type supplies one, and `openspore validate` then reports RETURN SEMANTICS PASS with the detail 'return type agrees with the bounded ABI record'. That agreement is between the source span and THIS FILE, not between the source and the machine -- the same self-validation the validator's own documentation refuses elsewhere. The machine-derived state is UNCLASSIFIED and stays that way; treat the PASS as a claim about internal consistency, not as a machine witness.
observed_original_abi.frame: none: no PUSH EBP, no MOV ESP,EBP, no SUB ESP. The body writes no register other than EAX and ECX, both scratch under every convention in play.
observed_original_abi.callee_side_stack_accounting: Two words enter the stack (PUSH EAX at 0x00b8de36 and 0x00b8de43) and two callees remove four bytes each (0x00ba6440 and 0x00ba6d80 both end `c2 04 00`, RET 4), so the entry's net stack effect is zero and its terminal RET is bare. Measured across the call in the model test and calibrated against control callees that pop 0 and 4 bytes.

field_offsets.grounding: categories.abi_derived.value.receiver: register ECX, shape R-DIRECT, offsets [388], max_offset 388, distinct_offsets 1, written_through 0, confidence INFERRED, bounds_only true. bounds_only is the record's own statement that its enumeration is open: it says where the body was SEEN reaching, not which member is which, and it cannot name a member. So the DISPLACEMENT is declared and nothing else -- an opaque byte run plus a displacement-named accessor, with the displacement a constexpr pinned by a static_assert to the instruction that states it. No struct, no member name, no offsetof, no class: a member name would be a layout claim no machine record here can corroborate.

layout.callee_set_source: knowledgegraph/triage/xrefs-2540f2ca.tsv read whole: four direct-call rows out of 0x00b8de30 (00b3d2a0 x2, 00ba6440, 00ba6d80) at callsites 0x00b8de37, 0x00b8de44, 0x00b8de3e, 0x00b8de4b. The index record's own dependencies.edges is edges_truncated true and projects only INCOMING rows (its 30-row window is entirely fan-in), so the export rather than the projection is the callee oracle here.
layout.push_ownership: Each PUSH is the argument of the call that FOLLOWS it, not of the 0x00b3d2a0 call it precedes. 0x00b3d2a0 reads no stack word and its terminator is a bare RET, so under every convention in which a callee cleans its own arguments a word pushed for it would have to be its argument -- and this callee neither reads nor removes it. 0x00ba6440 reads it (mov eax,[esp+4]) and removes it (ret 4); 0x00ba6d80 does the same (mov edx,[esp+4] ... ret 4). The arithmetic agrees: two PUSHes against two callee-side ret 4s is a net of zero, which is exactly what the bare terminal RET requires to leave the caller's frame intact. The same idiom appears twice, which is corroboration rather than proof.

globals_note: None, and the body really has none. The one memory operand is the receiver-relative read [ECX + 0x184]; the complete listing names no data-segment address. The global slot 0x0167eae4 that the accessor 0x00b3d2a0 reads belongs to THAT body, not this one, and is deliberately not named in the source: naming it would assert a data-segment reference out of 0x00b8de30 that this listing does not contain.

semantic_findings: The body is a four-call forwarding chain with one receiver read and no stores.

The receiver each thiscall callee receives is the ACCESSOR's return value, not the entry's own receiver: the two MOV ECX,EAX at 0x00b8de3c and 0x00b8de49 sit AFTER the accessor calls. A 'passes itself along' reconstruction is wrong here and the model test has a dedicated mutant for it.

The argument the second callee receives is the FIRST callee's return word, not the field: the PUSH at 0x00b8de43 pushes EAX, and EAX at that point holds 0x00ba6440's result. A second dedicated mutant conflates the two.

The accessor is called TWICE and both calls reach the same target (0x00b3d2a0); the two rel32 operands decode to the same address. A reconstruction that collapses them into one call is wrong and a third mutant says so.
Each PUSH belongs to the call that FOLLOWS it, not the one it precedes -- see layout.push_ownership.
not_claimed: The identity of the dword at receiver + 0x184. The receiver record is bounds_only and cannot name a member; no field name, class or layout is asserted.
The pointee type of the accessor's return value. The accessor's own global slot 0x0167eae4 is not named here and its semantics are not reconstructed here.
The semantics of 0x00b3d2a0, 0x00ba6440 or 0x00ba6d80. Only the values this body hands them are modelled.
That the function returns nothing in the ABI sense. The machine's last value-producing op is a CALL, the width is not determinable, and the validator classes that UNCLASSIFIED.

The identity of the 160 caller functions (index record) / 105 distinct callers (Ghidra get_function_by_address). A fan-in count is not a semantic classification; nothing here is inferred from who calls it.
Whether this function is a named SDK method. sdk_symbol is null and the SDK was not consulted for this target.

unresolved_questions: The C type of the return, and specifically whether the RETURN SEMANTICS PASS is worth anything. The machine's last value-producing op is a CALL, so the width is not determinable and the validator's must-analysis classes the state UNCLASSIFIED. A caller listing (0x00bbe608, `mov edi,eax` immediately after the call) shows at least one consumer reading EAX, so the body is not provably void at the ABI level. The declared void reflects that this body produces no value of its own, and the discrepancy is left open rather than resolved. Note also that the PASS is source-vs-THIS-SIDECAR agreement: the committed index record carries abi {}, so with no worker return_type on record the check is NOT_AVAILABLE.
What the dword at receiver + 0x184 denotes. The receiver record is bounds_only and no evidence in this package names the member.

Whether the two thiscall callees 0x00ba6440 and 0x00ba6d80 are members of one class, which would make this a two-step forward. 0x00ba6440 does not read ECX at all and 0x00ba6d80 reads two fields of it; that is a fact about those bodies and no claim is made about a shared class.

Why the record's dependencies.edges projects zero outgoing callees for this target. The export records four outgoing rows over three addresses, and the projection's 30-row window is spent entirely on the 160 incoming ones. CALLS reads the export whole and PASSes; the projection is a scheduler artefact and is not used as the callee oracle.
